name: Dylan Tan
tagline: Hardware products from first sketch to global launch: design, sourcing, testing and go-to-market.
contact_line: Have a product to bring to market?
about:
I'm a hardware product manager and industrial designer. I take physical products from the first sketch through sourcing, testing and launch, at every scale from a one-off public fountain to catalogs totaling more than 35,000 SKUs.

Most recently at C.R. Laurence I ran the product lifecycle for CRL's highest-revenue architectural, railing and transaction hardware, and took more than a dozen new products through CRL's stage-gate process. The last and largest was TurboFlex, a glass railing system brought from OnLevel in Europe through U.S. certification, Miami-Dade hurricane impact testing, a three-country supply chain and launch. Before that I led product development for more than 300 SKUs at Motech (Kitchen Bath Collection).

My background is hands-on. I studied 3-D Arts and Industrial Design at the University of Tennessee, I still prototype in metal, wood and concrete, model in Solidworks, Rhino and Blender, and build AI image pipelines in ComfyUI for marketing work.

experience.summary: End-to-end product lifecycle management across CRL's highest-revenue architectural, railing and transaction hardware. Led new products through the stage-gate process, from business case and forecasting to sourcing, certification, ERP setup and go-to-market, with 6+ programs running at once. My last and largest program was TurboFlex, a life-safety glass railing system brought from OnLevel in Europe through U.S. engineering review, ICC-ES evaluation and Miami-Dade hurricane impact testing to launch in six months.

Owned product development start to finish for 300+ SKUs in B2B and B2C. Worked directly with factories on material sourcing and OEM delivery, and bridged engineering, marketing and outside stakeholders through launch.
Designed and developed products around customer experience, pairing an industrial design background with data analysis across cross-functional teams.
Led product development for an OEM badge company, from modular clip systems to B2B and B2C packaging.
Designed and fabricated luxury goods for city contracts and commercial clients, including public water fountains, sculptures and home furnishings.
Remote CAD work for American-made goods under a mentor: my introduction to production and modern manufacturing.
